strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#64545 by building pandas at the buggy commit 9bc2fcf7171b, then running the developer's test_isin_mismatched_reso. On the buggy revision, 1-unit values at a finer resolution are truncated to the coarser self unit inside isin via as_unit(round_ok=True), so false matches return True. The test should fail for the three mismatched pairs where truncation occurs and pass once isin uses _ensure_matching_resos on the fixed revision. Versions are unbounded in the evidence, so the plan chooses a current NumPy and documents that choice.

pip_packages: numpy (latest release compatible with the buggy-era pandas dev tree; no documented or era-table constraint, so choice is ours)
tzdata (only needed on Windows/Emscripten; not required on Linux)
cython (latest; needed for source build; unbounded per evidence)
meson-python and meson (pandas pyproject build requirements; NOT in the evidence, included from general knowledge of the pandas build backend, verify against pyproject.toml at the buggy commit)
versioneer[toml] (pandas build-time dependency; NOT in the evidence, verify against pyproject.toml)
pytest (test runner; not in the evidence, needed to run the test)
system_packages: C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) and git, needed for the Cython and meson build; not stated in evidence

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arrays/test_datetimelike.py::test_isin_mismatched_reso, parametrized over dtype_kind in [M, m] and (self_unit, val_unit) in [(s,ns),(ms,us),(us,ns),(ns,s)]; each case builds self of unit self_unit with values [0,1], vals of unit val_unit with value [1], calls arr.isin(vals), and asserts tm.assert_numpy_array_equal against np.array([False, False])
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 9bc2fcf7171b, the three parametrizations (s,ns), (ms,us) and (us,ns) for both M and m must FAIL, because as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True truncates the val 1 (finer unit) to 0 in self's coarser unit, so index 0 matches and the result is [True, False] instead of [False, False]. The (ns,s) parametrizations are a control: no truncation is needed when casting the coarser values up, so they should PASS on both revisions. On the fixed revision (the PR merge that uses _ensure_matching_resos), all eight parametrizations must PASS, with the result exactly [False, False].
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import pandas as pd; dta=pd.array(pd.to_datetime(['2020-01-01']).as_unit('s')); vals=pd.array(pd.to_datetime(['2020-01-01 00:00:00.000000001']).as_unit('ns')); print(dta.isin(vals))"  (buggy: [True]; fixed: [False])
risks: The buggy behaviour is pure Python/Cython logic in the datetimelike isin path and is not architecture-, sanitiser- or threading-dependent, so Linux x86_64 with a standard build should reproduce it; no platform-specific behaviour is evidenced.
The (ns,s) parametrizations do not transition: they pass on the buggy revision too, so the transition is defined only by the other three resolution pairs for each dtype kind.
The fixed-revision commit hash is not given in the evidence; check out the PR merge commit for PR #64545 and confirm it contains the _ensure_matching_resos change.

Editable install (-ve) lets Python-level changes take effect after checkout without a full rebuild, but if checkout moves Cython files, a rebuild is needed; rebuild after switching revisions to be safe.

Build requirements beyond cython (meson-python, versioneer, a C compiler) are not in the evidence and must be taken from the buggy commit's pyproject.toml; a mismatch will block the build before the test can run.

Test uses DatetimeArray and TimedeltaArray _from_sequence with explicit dtype; if the test module at the buggy commit lacks these imports or the signature differs, the test errors rather than fails on the bug, which would not be a valid transition.

NumPy version is unbounded in evidence; a very new NumPy may conflict with the buggy-era pandas tree. Pin to a NumPy release from the same era as the commit if the build or import fails, and record that choice.
The regression test comment references GH64545 with a possible placeholder in a draft; this does not affect execution.
No tolerance applies: the comparison is exact boolean equality through tm.assert_numpy_array_equal, so the oracle is exact.

oracle.why: isin returns boolean membership; a correct result has no floating-point component and must match exactly.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: For the (s,ns), (ms,us), (us,ns) parametrizations, the buggy as_unit(self.unit) truncates the value 1 in the finer unit to 0 in the coarser unit, so arr's 0 matches and the assertion sees [True, False] where [False, False] is expected, which fails tm.assert_numpy_array_equal.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With _ensure_matching_resos casting both arrays up to the finer unit, value 1 at finer resolution never equals 0 or 1 at the coarser unit, so the result is [False, False] and all eight parametrizations pass.
